To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
perinatal (PER) or early post‐natal (EPN) Pb exposure had different effects on learning and memory depending on the strain (LE vs. SD), sex, and timing of exposure.

the effects of Pb acetates exposure on learning and recall are differentially associated with timing of Pb exposure, sex, the strain (Long Evans or Sprague Dawley) of the exposed rat, and the specific behavioral test (memory consolidation vs. recall) being evaluated.

the effects of low level Pb acetate exposure in early life on hippocampus dependent learning and memory are strain (LE orSD) and sex dependent, and are differentially associated with timing of the Pb‐exposure, PERI (gestation to postnatal 21) or EPN (postnatal day 1‐21).
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms by which genetic factors influence the response to developmental lead (Pb2+) exposure, which is a significant public health issue.
the effects of low level, developmental exposure to lead (PBL) on learning and memory in two strains of rats (Long Evans and Sprague Dawley) and the influence of sex and timing of exposure.
understanding how genetic background and developmental timing interact to influence the functional outcomes of developmental lead exposure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Pb exposure has significant strain‐specific effects on learning and memory, with the effects being dependent on the timing of exposure, sex and genetic background.

the effects of Pb acetates exposure on learning and/or memory were differentially affected by the timing of exposure (PERI and EPN), sex of the exposed animal, and the strain of the animal (LE or SD).
the effects of Pb on hippocampus‐dependent associative learning and memory are strain‐specific.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the strain‐specific effects of Pb exposure on hippocampal function are associated with a differential effect on gene expression patterns.
the effects of Pb on learning and memory are differentially associated with timing of Pb exposure, sex, genetic background, and the behavioral measure used.
Pb exposure during early development can differentially affect learning and memory depending on the timing of exposure, sex of the animal, and the genetic background of the animal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic background of the exposed animal can influence both the behavioral and molecular effects of Pb exposure.
the effects of early life Pb exposure on gene transcription in the brain are strain specific.
the effects of low level Pb exposure on the developing brain may be modulated by the genetic background of the exposed individual.
